newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurds end clash, ceasefire takes hold.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds end clash, ceasefire takes hold.

text.p: Rival Kurdish militias clashed for five hours near a northern Iraqi town on Thursday despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that appeared to have silenced guns in the rest of the mountainous region.

Witnesses said the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) traded shots near the town of Degala after the PUK launched an attack in mid-morning. But fighting halted in the afternoon.
"We would have brought in our heavy weapons but the PUK stopped," leading KDP commander Roj Nuri Shuwayis told Reuters.
The PUK had fired Katyusha rockets and artillery at KDP positions near the KDP-held Degala while Shuwayis' forces responded with heavy machine-gun fire. Neither group advanced from their positions.
The U.S. State Department announced that the groups had agreed to observe a ceasefire beginning at midnight Iraqi time (2000 GMT on Wednesday).

U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau got an agreement to halt the fighting from the two factions' leaders at separate meetings in Turkey this week. The clashes have damaged U.S. interests in northern Iraq and threatened to draw in Iraq and Iran.
Iraqi troops and tanks helped the KDP capture Arbil from the PUK on August 31, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes against Iraqi military targets.
